about: Language-neutral contract of the portico-transport IPC (the Rust binary in transport-rs/; it also covers the former Go binary, whose source `transport/` was deleted after the cut-over, D-20261123-cc1e, and is in git history at commit bdd8e61). Derived on 2026-11-13 from transport/cmd/portico-transport/main.go, internal/ipc/*.go and the Go binary's own answers (wire_cases / empty_hub_errors were generated from the Go binary and read against main.go), then checked against the Rust binary. Where the two binaries differ, the difference is a row of `implementation_differences` that names its PARITY.md entry; it is never a spec choice. Executed by transport-rs/scripts/contract_runner.py against the Rust binary (the Go binary can no longer be built; the Go `go` fields below are the frozen reference). Request/notification shapes are the contract; the free-text of Go's errors (json.Unmarshal wording) is part of it because the Python side logs it.

transport.unix: newline-delimited JSON on a unix socket created 0600, ONE connection served; the process exits when it closes
transport.tcp: -listen: same framing after an auth line; reconnects allowed; see requests.auth

framing.line_limit_note: a line plus its newline must fit in 1 MiB; 1048575 content bytes served, 1048576 fails the serve loop (exit 1, socket file left behind)
dropped_silently: id not an integer literal (1.5, 1e2, strings)
framing.zero_request: the JSON literal null is a zero request: unknown_method, id 0, message empty
framing.keys: case-insensitive (ASCII), duplicates: last wins, null fields ignored, missing id is 0
framing.string_escaping: Go encoding/json: \u003c \u003e \u0026 \u2028 \u2029, short escapes \b \f \n \r \t, other controls \u00xx
framing.order: plain handlers run concurrently (responses matched by id); inline handlers (media_*) run on the read loop in arrival order; keyed handlers serialise per key in arrival order

params.driver: string, one of the drivers below

configure.notes: a configure of an id already present is already_configured; the reply precedes driver_availability when the event is raised from the driver's own task, but an event raised inside Start precedes the reply (PARITY 301; the transcripts keep the real order)

result.call_id: string, only for drivers with a call-placing dial (gate_sip_observer, gate_sip_server)

keepalive.notes: always not_implemented: Phase 1: keepalive/hangup tracking not built yet (§9.5)

webrtc_offer.notes: joins the pending ring of that call id; the answer is G.722 else PCMU

params.stats: bool, optional (DEV-811 P3): true asks for the leg's counters in media_closed; absent or anything but true = off

media_open.notes: 5 s without a frame closes the leg: media_closed reason idle. Since slice 8 the leg is joined to its call's device leg

media_close.notes: media_closed is notified BEFORE the response; an unknown leg is {ok:true}. DEV-811 P3: call_audio_stats is sent only by a gate_sip_server configured with call_stats:true, once per answered call at the end of its audio; the configure reply of that driver lists Features [call_stats]

house_open.dispatch: keyed (call_id) when -house-calls is on, plain when it is off (main.go registers Handle, then HandleKeyed)
house_open.notes: default OFF (-house-calls); cap 4 bridges, per-owner cap

house_close.dispatch: keyed (call_id) when -house-calls is on, plain when it is off

auth.notes: must arrive within 5 s; anything else drops the connection; not available on the unix socket

media_closed.stats: object, only when media_open said stats:true (DEV-811 P3): uplink_frames, uplink_bad_frame, uplink_full_drops, downlink_frames, downlink_send_ms_max, uplink_gap_ms_max, uplink_gap_ms_p95 (counts and milliseconds)

call_audio_stats.station_frames: int, station frames the downlink saw
call_audio_stats.pre_gain_hist: 31 ints: per-frame peak before the x4 gain, 3 dB bins; bin 0 below -90 dBFS, bin i (1..30) covers [-93+3i, -90+3i) dBFS, bin 30 holds full scale
call_audio_stats.would_clip_frames: int, frames whose pre-gain peak would clip at x4
call_audio_stats.saturated_samples: int, samples at +-full scale (both signs) as they leave the server
call_audio_stats.queued_to_app, dropped_to_app, received_: int, the call's own queue counters

notifications_note: notifications go out only while a client is connected; a ring before the connection exists is not replayed

gate_sip_observer.note: no claims, no dial: it listens only

gate_sip_observer+claims+dial.note: claims_enabled and dial_enabled: audio is carried by the claim; CanDial

capabilities_note: Capabilities is marshalled in struct order InboundAudio, OutboundAudio, DirectCapable, HasRelay, RTSPTemplate, ReportsAvailability, then CanDial only when true (checked in the raw lines of the transcripts). InboundAudio/OutboundAudio are driver.AudioTopology: 0 SIPRTP, 1 InVideoStream, 2 TalkbackPush, 3 NoAudio. capabilities_changed repeats the object after a start-up republish (observer/talk with dial).

log.stream: stdout and stderr both used by Go; hub.py merges and drains both; Rust writes to stderr only (PARITY 87)
log.house_call_summary: portico-transport: house call <call_id> ended reason=<reason> cause=<cause> dur=<duration>

exit_codes.2: flag parse error (also the Go runtime exit code of an unrecovered panic)

soft_contracts.restart_policy: hub.py restarts the process once; a unix-mode client disconnect is an exit 0 that hub.py sees as an unexpected exit

socket.mode: 0600 (bind then chmod: a window with 0777&~umask exists in both)
socket.stale: a file at the path is removed first

signals.SIGINT: stop accepting, close the connection, stop drivers, remove socket, exit 0

wheel_features.note: Python-side feature detection; not a binary behaviour

panic_policy.go: there is NO recover() in the non-test Go sources (grep of transport/ 2026-11-13): a panic in any goroutine ends the process (runtime exit 2, trace on stderr) and hub.py restarts it once. The plan and PARITY text that speak of Go recover() sites do not match the code.
panic_policy.rust: panic = unwind (Cargo.toml). A panic in a tokio task is contained to that task (supervised drivers restart their loop; a call-carrying task ends THAT call and reports an end), call-carrying tasks run under catch_unwind with guaranteed teardown; a panic on the main thread aborts the process. panic_hook::install() prints 'portico-transport: panic at <file>:<line>: <payload>' first (PARITY 155).
panic_policy.why_not_a_runner_case: no request makes either binary panic on purpose; the policy is pinned by the Rust unit tests that inject a panic (tests/panic_hook.rs, talk_panics.rs, sfu_session.rs, house.rs) and by PARITY rows sip difference 4, 88, 97, 102, 113, 114, 131, 145, 157, 166, 175

implementation_differences.go: has host candidates: True; end-of-candidates: True; ice-ufrag: True; ice-pwd: True; fingerprint: True; setup: \['a=setup:active'\]; rtcp-mux: True
implementation_differences.rust: has host candidates: True; end-of-candidates: True; ice-ufrag: True; ice-pwd: True; fingerprint: True; setup: \['a=setup:passive'\]; rtcp-mux: True
implementation_differences.note: Go (pion) is the DTLS client, Rust (str0m) the server; both interoperate (INTEROP.md)
the /1 channel suffix is removed from the offer before str0m parses it and not written back
Go keeps the session of a refused first offer in the registry (candidate/answer then fail as webrtc_failed); Rust drops it (unknown_session)

implementation_differences.rust: \| portico-transport: warning: the -secrets-env file is readable by group or others \(mode 0[0-7]{3}\); restrict it to its owner
implementation_differences.note: Rust warns when the .env file is group/other readable; Go reads whatever it is pointed at and says nothing (the line of the transcript's log section; the same text inside the process-output line is covered by DIFF-STANDALONE-LOG-LINES)

parity: Other differences: Rust cannot hold ... a lone \ud800 escape in a decoded string: such a request line is dropped
implementation_differences.note: Go replaces the lone surrogate with U+FFFD and answers; Rust drops the whole line (no response). Row 161 fixed the field strings the dispatcher reads, not the request line itself

implementation_differences.go: process output: '<TIME> gate_sip_server: SIP on 127\.0\.0\.1:<SIPPORT>, RTP on :<RTP>, realm "VDP", user "8001", ring limit 45s, orphan grace 15s\\n'
implementation_differences.rust: process output: '(portico-transport: warning: the -secrets-env file is readable by group or others \(mode 0[0-7]{3}\); restrict it to its owner\\n)?<TIME> gate_sip_server: SIP on 127\.0\.0\.1:<SIPPORT>, RTP on :<RTP>, realm "VDP", user "8001", ring limit 45s, orphan grace 15s\\n(portico-transport: ipc: refused a TCP connection from 127\.0\.0\.1: no valid auth line\\n)?'
implementation_differences.note: the process-output lines of the standalone flow, matched as whole lines: the Go line is the SIP start line only; the Rust line may add the mode warning (DIFF-STANDALONE-ENV-MODE-WARNING, parity 186) before it and the refused-connection line (parity 188) after it

a REGISTER with Expires 0: Go answers Expires 300 and registers, Rust de-registers (the Contact expiry wins); proven by the retired scripts/wire_deferred.py (DEV-831; conformance/deferred_wire_results.json)
a nonce issued to one host is refused from another host in Rust, accepted by Go
a CANCEL for a live call from a different source host is refused in Rust, ends the call in Go
a BYE for a live call from a different source host is refused in Rust, ends the call in Go
the same for a call the transport dialled
SIGTERM during a TCP auth window: Go waits for the window (3 s and more), Rust exits at once
an ICMP port-unreachable deafens a Go endpoint for good; Rust keeps reading
an offer over 64 KiB is refused in Rust; a=end-of-candidates is accepted in Rust, an error in Go
a panic in a handler: Go exits (runtime exit 2), Rust answers internal_error / `handler panicked` and keeps serving

the TCP listener: Rust accepts all the time, at most 4 waiting, the newest authenticated hub replaces the served one, three wrong tokens from one source are slowed (Go serves one connection at a time in the accepting goroutine)
a config nested deeper than 128 is bad_params in Rust (serde_json's limit); Go accepts up to 10 000
a non-UTF-8 command-line argument: Rust exits 2, Go uses the bytes
the 33rd remote candidate of a session is refused in Rust
a session request after the shutdown started: `sfu: the transport is stopping` in Rust
Rust sends driver_error with the code `socket_failed` when the gate_sip_server read loop gives up; Go never sends that code (see driver_error_codes)

driver_error_codes.note: Go: only the dahua driver sends driver_error, with `registration_failed` (grep of transport/ for DriverError, 2026-11-13; the reviewer's `register_failed` does not exist). Rust adds `socket_failed` (gate_sip_server, PARITY 330). Both send the fields device_id, message, code.
